ranked_facts.why: The presence of hypercalcemia, as indicated by the serum Ca2+ level of 12.5 mg/dL, is more strongly associated with primary hyperparathyroidism (B4) than with gastrointestinal disorders (B2), as the latter would not typically cause such a significant elevation in calcium levels without other underlying conditions being present.

Hypophosphatemia, as seen with a serum phosphorus level of 2.0 mg/dL, is more characteristic of primary hyperparathyroidism (B4) due to the increased parathyroid hormone levels leading to phosphate excretion, rather than being a direct consequence of gastrointestinal disorders (B2).
